top_signals.title: U.S. warns allies of missile delivery delays due to shortage
top_signals.summary: Multiple European nations are expecting deliveries of key missile and air defense capabilities to be pushed back as a result of the Iran war.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Chancellor announces Bank of England appointments
top_signals.summary: His Majesty the King and the Chancellor have appointed three new non-executive directors to the Bank of England’s Court of Directors.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Central-bank repricing affecting yields, FX, liquidity and equities.

top_signals.title: Labour warned UK at risk of foreign tech giants ‘pulling the plug’
top_signals.summary: Labour has “no plan” if foreign technology companies or governments cut Britain off from systems underpinning critical services, the Liberal Democrats have warned, after ministers acknowledged the risks posed by the UK’s reliance on overseas tech. top_signals.title: Flawed AI-linked intel almost led U.S. to board China ship, report says
top_signals.summary: The operation was called off after officials determined that an AI chatbot used by an analyst had misidentified the material the ship was carrying.

top_signals.title: US Air Force has a $14 billion supply hole, service officials say
top_signals.summary: As the force grapples with supply chain and maintenance issues, sustainment funding to fill the $14 billion gap is becoming increasingly necessary.

top_signals.summary: The service lives of the B-1 Lancer and B-2 Spirit will be extended, with their pilots to be some of the first to fly the B-21 Raider.

top_signals.title: Nations take action on North Korean IT workers after UN report
top_signals.summary: A report published Wednesday said that as of July, Vietnam, Laos, Pakistan and Argentina took meaningful steps to respond to allegations involving North Korea listed in an October study.

top_signals.title: Activities of U.S. Affiliates of Foreign Multinational Enterprises, 2024
top_signals.summary: Majority-owned U.S. affiliates of foreign multinational enterprises employed 8.57 million workers in the United States in 2024, a 0.2 percent increase from 8.56 million workers in 2023, according to statistics on U.S. affiliate operations and finances released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis.
